findings.summary: `set -u` only errors on *unset* parameters, so it does not catch the described case where `DIR` is set to an empty string.
findings.evidence: "`set -u` catches `rm -rf $DIR/` when `DIR` is empty." — Bash manual, `set -u`: "Treat unset variables and parameters other than the special parameters '@' or '*'... as an error when performing parameter expansion." `DIR=""` is set, so `rm -rf $DIR/` expands to `rm -rf /` with no error under `set -u`.
findings.fix: Change the bullet to "`set -u` catches `rm -rf $DIR/` when `DIR` is **unset** — not when it is set to empty; use `rm -rf "${DIR:?DIR is empty}"/` to cover both."

findings.summary: The claim that `set -e` "never" fires inside `&&` or `||` is wrong for the command following the final `&&`/`||`, which does trigger an exit.
findings.evidence: "`set -e` never fires inside `if`, `while`, `&&`, `||` or `!`." — Bash manual, `set -e`: the shell does not exit if the failing command is "part of any command executed in a && or || list **except the command following the final && or ||**". So under `set -e`, `true && false` exits the shell.
findings.fix: Reword to "`set -e` is suppressed in `if`/`while` tests, in `!` pipelines, and in every `&&`/`||` stage **except the last one** — `true && false` still exits."

findings.summary: Chapter 7 (exit status / pipefail) is split across pages 1 and 4 with the Scope and Common-Mistakes chapters wedged in between, so the learner meets the topic, leaves it for two pages, and returns.
findings.evidence: Page 1 title "Exit Status, set -e and pipefail" (exit-status table, `set -euo pipefail`), then page 2 "Scope: Blocks, Loops, Functions, exec", page 3 "Wrong Turns: Order, Quoting and sudo", then page 4 "Silent Failures: PIPESTATUS and ERR Traps" returns to `set -o pipefail`, `set -e`, `set -u`, `PIPESTATUS`.
findings.fix: Reorder so the two exit-status pages are adjacent: page 1 (exit status table, `set -e`/`-u`/pipefail semantics) → page 4 content (PIPESTATUS, pipefail gotcha, ERR trap, strict header) → Scope → Common Mistakes → Recap.

findings.summary: The stated error message for trailing whitespace after a heredoc terminator is not what Bash emits.
findings.evidence: "Trailing whitespace after the terminator: `unexpected end of file`." — Bash actually emits `warning: here-document at line N delimited by end-of-file (wanted `EOF')` and silently swallows the rest of the script as heredoc body; the script still runs and exits 0.
findings.fix: Change to "Trailing whitespace after the terminator: the delimiter is not recognised — Bash warns `here-document ... delimited by end-of-file (wanted 'EOF')` and eats the rest of the script."

findings.summary: The summary table labels enabling pipefail as `+pipefail`, but in shell `set +` *disables* an option (and `set +pipefail` is not valid syntax — it needs `-o`/`+o`).
findings.evidence: Table rows: ["`set -e`","a simple command failing"], ["`+pipefail`","any stage of a pipeline"] — `set +o pipefail` turns pipefail off; `set -o pipefail` turns it on.
findings.fix: Rename the row to `set -eo pipefail` (or `-o pipefail`) so the sign matches the shell's meaning.

findings.summary: Pushpin graphics are drawn on top of code text in three blocks, obscuring characters.
findings.evidence: Pin covers "ERR" in `trap 'echo died $LINENO' ERR`, the "n" of "# next line" in `st=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}")  # next line`, and "SIGPIPE" in `# head quits → producer SIGPIPE`.
findings.fix: Offset the sticky-note pin so it anchors below the final code line rather than over it, or add bottom padding inside code blocks that carry a pinned note.

findings.summary: "Add `wait`" is presented as a general fix for truncated `>(cmd)` output, but bare `wait` covers only the last process substitution and will hang when the writer's fd is still held open by `exec`.
findings.evidence: "`>(cmd)` output may be incomplete when the script exits." / "Add `wait` before you read what the writer produced." — Bash manual, `wait`: "If no options or ids are supplied, wait waits for all running background jobs and **the last-executed process substitution, if its process id is the same as `$!`**, and the return status is zero." With `tee >(a) >(b)` only one is waited for, and after `exec > >(tee -a run.log)` (page 2) `tee` never exits until the shell's fd 1 is closed, so `wait` blocks.
findings.fix: Qualify it: "Capture `pid=$!` right after the process substitution and `wait "$pid"`; bare `wait` only covers the last one. For `exec > >(tee ...)`, close/restore the fd (`exec 1>&3 3>&-`) before waiting or `tee` never exits."
